claim.anchor: Ouro Preto Imperial Topaz veins, Minas Gerais, Brazil (Variant B per Morteani et al. 2002).
claim.description: Hydrothermal topaz vein in Precambrian phyllite + quartzite. Single clean cooling curve from 360°C to 50°C — the 'anti-flash-quench' of the gem-pegmatite scenarios. F-pulse gates topaz nucleation; Cr leach commits the imperial color.

deterministic.reason: A plausible product of sodic phyllite/feldspar alteration in the Ouro Preto metamorphic-hydrothermal vein.
A subordinate wall-rock alteration/gangue phase derived from the feldspathic component of the host sequence.

deterministic_accessory.reason: A plausible product of sodic phyllite/feldspar alteration in the Ouro Preto metamorphic-hydrothermal vein.

aspirational.reason: A plausible late oxidizing Fe-weathering product after the imperial-topaz vein cools, but absent from all three SIM 272 commissioned seeds.
Hydrated silica is a plausible late low-temperature competitor after the main topaz-quartz stage, but absent from all three SIM 272 commissioned seeds.
A minor late Fe-oxyhydroxide remains permitted during terminal oxidation, subordinate to goethite, but is absent from all three SIM 272 commissioned seeds.
Morteani et al. describe imperial topaz in quartz-hematite veins, but the current authored path produces no discrete hematite in the three SIM 272 commissioned seeds.

sources: Morteani et al. 2002 — fluid inclusion microthermometry of Ouro Preto Imperial Topaz veins
notes: Hydrothermal veins cutting Precambrian phyllite and quartzite in the Ouro Preto district. Fluid inclusion data (Morteani et al. 2002) puts crystallization at ~360°C, 3.5 kbar from metamorphic brines derived from devolatilization of phyllite.
Single clean cooling curve — 360°C → 50°C — the anti-flash-quench of the gem-pegmatite scenarios. No thermal events, no pressure spikes. One exhalation from the granite cooling below.

The gate: topaz can't nucleate until fluorine accumulates past a saturation threshold. Early quartz grows alone. A mid-scenario metamorphic dehydration event (step 35) pumps F from the phyllite micas into the fluid, and the vein transitions to imperial topaz territory. The imperial color — golden-orange to pink — depends on Cr3+ dissolved out of nearby ultramafic bodies; without chromium the topaz is colorless or pale blue.

Audit gap-fills (Apr 2026): Na=60, K=40 (phyllite muscovite/albite breakdown per Morteani 2002). Mg=15 (phyllite chlorite/biotite, brief-required non-zero baseline; conservative since host is quartzite + phyllite, not mafic).
